100 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

The teacher, with a look of amazement upon his face, would call out, "Keep quiet back there, boys!" and for the time being Bill would release his string, and in a few minutes he would commence again, to the amusement of the teacher. News items told of frequent visits of the business manager to notify delinquent subscribers. About the time the teacher faced around, looking squarely at the class, the noise would cease, and even search the desks to find the origin of it. Bill replied, "Yes, Sir."

Montgomery challenged, "Then let us hear it." Bill arose and commenced with a ring of inflection on each "Woe" and delivered his recitation in such a decided note of awareness, stand out more boldly in the memory.

Finally Montgomery stopped and listened at it for a moment and then said, "What is that making that noise?"

Bill replied, "I do not know, Sir; it is in the wall, I reckon."

Finally the mystery was solved and turned out to be Bill's; and the entire class was given a sound thrashing. This was duly written to the episode of the scholar in The Platonian Messenger.

Here is another good one, with the same principal involved:

For the subject was Elocution, a practice of reading sentences taken at random from the reader; the teacher called upon some of the various students I do not recall to give his rendition of the sentence, "Woe!"
